mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month indicates a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence increase.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity (HOUST) over the last two months signals a strengthening demand side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the housing market is a leading indicator of economic health.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST showed a sustained increase over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last month signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it indicates a strong consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending drives corporate revenues.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a falling consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over the last two months suggests a potential disinflationary environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real interest rates improve.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase & CPIAUCSL decrease in 2 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased and CPIAUCSL decreased over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in the last month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points, signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as employment growth boosts consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k & UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2 percentage points in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over the last quarter, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points, signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth boosts corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase & UNRATE decrease > 0.3pp in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 increased and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3 percentage points over the last quarter.
